page: Google Cloud Platform c3-highcpu-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 4 vCPUs and 8 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8481C processor running at 2.7 GHz, this x86_64 architecture server allocates 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled (2 threads per core). It features a dedicated CPU allocation with 48 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a 105 MB L3 cache. The instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear division between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is average, as demonstrated by a stress-ng single-core score of 1620.59 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1635.0. However, multi-core and memory-bound operations lean toward the weaker end of the spectrum. The Geekbench multi-core score is 3703.0, and the Passmark CPU score is 6115.19, both falling into the bottom 25% of benchmarked systems. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with uncached read and write speeds of 27.54 GB/sec and 21.03 GB/sec respectively, resulting in a poor Passmark memory score of 989.87.

From a workload perspective, the c3-highcpu-4 is appropriate for compute-bound tasks that do not require substantial memory footprints or high-throughput parallel processing. It performs adequately in single-threaded operations like gzip compression (25.97 GB/sec) and static web serving (6.78 GB/sec throughput). However, it is less effective for memory-intensive database operations, complex software compilation, or heavy multi-threaded decompression. The hardware profile offers qualitative cost efficiency for dedicated Intel Xeon compute resources when memory requirements are strictly capped at 2 GB per vCPU.
